items.next_action: None. ACP-001 is closed on an independent read-only Codex PASS against frozen SHA 907447a20c93c60483e1e6a0156e49964cd7e539. Do not reopen without contradictory evidence; the kernel is now the execution authority for every later item.

Transition recorded: RUNNING_JUDGE -> JUDGE_FAIL after structured Codex FAIL; repair is now explicitly queued and bounded to the three P1 findings.
Transition recorded: JUDGE_FAIL -> REPAIR_READY; bounded repair approved by the active Control Plane program.
Transition recorded: REPAIR_READY -> RUNNING_WRITER; exactly one Claude/Opus repair writer requested in GitHub Actions.

REPAIR P1-1 fixed: kernel.mjs now audits the ENTIRE committed schema for unsupported keywords before looking at the board value (assertSchemaSupported), so a constraint on an absent property, under items of an empty array, or in an unused object-form additionalProperties can no longer be silently skipped. Schema-pointer diagnostics; no schema file change was required.

REPAIR P1-2 fixed: new guardJudgePassRequiresVerdict rejects RUNNING_JUDGE -> JUDGE_PASS without an explicit PASS verdict (JUDGE_PASS_WITHOUT_VERDICT), a FAIL verdict (JUDGE_PASS_CONTRADICTS_VERDICT), and an unknown verdict (UNKNOWN_JUDGE_VERDICT). UNVERIFIABLE still stops at UNVERIFIABLE_MANDATORY_GATE via the pre-existing upstream guard; UNVERIFIABLE != PASS is preserved.

REPAIR P1-3 fixed: checkActivePrograms layers now accumulate instead of returning early, which made MULTIPLE_ACTIVE_PROGRAMS reachable rather than dead code, and the suite gained a removal proof, a per-layer proof, and an inversion proof for the exactly-one-active-program guard. The original direct two-canonical-board negative test is retained.

Tests added for the repair: 3 P1-1 negative cases plus a non-object-subschema case, a whole-schema-audit reverse proof, and a committed-schema enforceability case; 2 P1-2 direct negative cases plus a reverse proof and an inversion proof; 4 P1-3 cases covering both layers, board-level halt, discovery, removal, per-layer and inversion proofs. The pre-existing UNVERIFIABLE reverse proof was strengthened (not weakened) so it stays non-vacuous now that a second layer stands behind it.
node --test control-plane/*.test.mjs after repair: 67 pass, 0 fail (was 50 before the repair); no test was deleted or relaxed.
node control-plane/kernel.mjs check after repair: ok=true, violation_count=0, exit code 0; next_action=ADVANCE_IN_FLIGHT for ACP-001.

Repair scope honoured: only control-plane/kernel.mjs, control-plane/kernel.test.mjs and this board changed. No dependency added, no product or clinical code touched, no deployment behaviour changed, .github/** untouched, no commit or push performed by the writer.

Transition recorded: RUNNING_WRITER -> WRITER_DONE after the bounded three-P1 repair passed focused verification. JUDGE_PASS and CLOSED remain unclaimed; a fresh independent Codex audit on a newly frozen SHA is required.

Transition recorded: SHA_FROZEN -> RUNNING_JUDGE; one independent Codex re-audit is authorized against frozen SHA 907447a20c93c60483e1e6a0156e49964cd7e539.
Judge requirements preserved: CODEX_INDEPENDENT, read-only, UNVERIFIABLE != PASS, no merge, no deploy, no PHI.

Independent Codex judge workflow run 31951393592 job 95175279018 completed with conclusion SUCCESS; permissions were contents:read, actions:read, pull-requests:read and the Codex action ran with permission-profile ':read-only' and safety-strategy drop-sudo.

Structured Codex verdict on frozen SHA 907447a20c93c60483e1e6a0156e49964cd7e539: PASS. Verbatim verdict preserved in control-plane/verdicts/acp001-codex-verdict-31951393592.json (immutable artifact acp001-codex-verdict-31951393592, artifact id 9264790890, zip sha256 4641d64b382e1bc83ef243fb4aa125ba46521172305b62907788a6075f000194, retained by GitHub only until 2026-09-15, therefore committed here).

Verdict preconditions verified before any transition: audited_sha == 907447a20c93c60483e1e6a0156e49964cd7e539 (the exact frozen candidate), independent == true, read_only == true, verdict within {PASS, FAIL, UNVERIFIABLE}. The judge workflow enforced the same four conditions in-run via jq before persisting the artifact.

All twelve mandatory gates returned PASS: schema_validation, single_active_program, single_active_writer, deterministic_selection, transition_table, owner_policy_invariants, writer_lock, unverifiable_not_pass, p2_p3_no_auto_repair, legacy_authority_rejected, reverse_mutation_proof, focused_tests. findings == [] — no P0, no blocking P1, and no non-blocking P2/P3 was raised.

Audit integrity proved by the run itself: the judge checked out the frozen candidate with persist-credentials:false, asserted HEAD == 907447a2 with an empty worktree before auditing, and proved orchestration_head_at_start == orchestration_head_at_end == 8def4b841771a98955ff08aa36fbaf8f80e41003, so SHA_CHANGED_DURING_AUDIT did not occur.

Transition recorded: RUNNING_JUDGE -> JUDGE_PASS. Proved legal by the kernel itself under the real verdict context — evaluateTransition('RUNNING_JUDGE','JUDGE_PASS',{judge_verdict:'PASS',judge_independent:true,judge_read_only:true}) returns ok=true, and statusForJudgeVerdict('PASS') independently maps the verdict to JUDGE_PASS.

Transition recorded: JUDGE_PASS -> CLOSED. evaluateTransition('JUDGE_PASS','CLOSED', same context) returns ok=true; guardClosureRequiresIndependentJudge accepted it only because verdict==PASS, judge_independent==true and judge_read_only==true were all present.

No state was skipped: evaluateTransition('RUNNING_JUDGE','CLOSED', same context) is rejected with SKIPPED_STATE ('skips 1 required state(s)'), so closure could not have been reached without passing through JUDGE_PASS. The board therefore travelled READY -> RUNNING_WRITER -> WRITER_DONE -> CI_PENDING -> SHA_FROZEN -> RUNNING_JUDGE -> JUDGE_FAIL -> REPAIR_READY -> RUNNING_WRITER -> WRITER_DONE -> CI_PENDING -> SHA_FROZEN -> RUNNING_JUDGE -> JUDGE_PASS -> CLOSED with every edge in the transition table.

Required CI for the audited artefact is CI #1018 run 31924253766 on the exact frozen SHA 907447a20c93c60483e1e6a0156e49964cd7e539: SUCCESS across all five jobs. The closure commit does not alter control-plane/kernel.mjs, control-plane/MASTER_BOARD.schema.json, or any product, clinical or deployment file, so the audited BEHAVIOUR is byte-identical to what Codex judged.

P3 (non-blocking, found while closing, not present in the Codex findings): the focused-test fixture `readyBoard()` was value-coupled to live board state. It rewound ACP-001 to READY without rewinding the items that depend on ACP-001, so the first legal advance past ACP-001 made the fixture itself incoherent and the kernel correctly rejected it with BLOCKED_BY_OUT_OF_SYNC. The kernel was right and the fixture was wrong; the two failing cases were 'happy path: exactly one eligible item is selected deterministically' and 'happy path: an in-flight item is advanced, never replaced by a second writer'. Fixed forward inside control-plane/kernel.test.mjs by making the rewind generic — every item after ACP-001 returns to QUEUED with a truthful blocker list. No guard, no assertion and no expected violation code was changed, added or relaxed; the suite still holds 67 cases. Per the execution policy a P3 does not open a repair loop, so this is recorded as evidence rather than escalated.

The fixture fix also restored a proof that had gone vacuous: 'dependency violation: blocked_by must tell the truth about open dependencies' sets ACP-002's blockers to [], which is only a real mutation while the fixture actually declares ACP-001 as a blocker.

Closure verification re-run on the closing tree: node --test control-plane/*.test.mjs -> 67 pass, 0 fail; node control-plane/kernel.mjs check -> ok=true, violation_count=0, exit code 0. Reverse-proved: the pre-fix fixture against the post-closure board fails 2 of 67, so the fixture change is load-bearing and not cosmetic.
No forbidden action was taken to close: no merge, no deploy, no PHI, no destructive change, no clinical-policy change, no secret rotation, no product or clinical code touched.

items.title: Cloud writer runner
items.next_action: Build the bounded, least-privilege cloud writer runner: a fail-closed preflight implementing the thirteen BASELINE.md conditions as testable code, and one GitHub Actions workflow that runs exactly one writer against the deterministically selected item and can neither deploy to production nor merge to main.
evidence: Unblocked by the closure of ACP-001 on independent Codex PASS (run 31951393592, frozen SHA 907447a20c93c60483e1e6a0156e49964cd7e539). The dependency is met, so `blocked_by` may no longer name ACP-001 — the kernel rejects a closed item left standing as a blocker (BLOCKED_BY_OUT_OF_SYNC).

FROZEN_ORCHESTRATION_SHA=8cda1aac5c59749e2196f7fbde6eed1334c8f067 — the immutable post-closure orchestration state ACP-002 starts from. At that SHA ACP-001 is CLOSED with its closer recorded, the board validates with zero violations, and the focused suite is 67/67.

Transition recorded: QUEUED -> READY. evaluateTransition('QUEUED','READY') returns ok=true, and the unblocking is real rather than declared: ACP-001 is CLOSED, so ACP-002's dependency is met and its blocker list is legitimately empty.

Transition recorded: READY -> RUNNING_WRITER. acquireWriterLock(NO_LOCK,{item_id:'ACP-002',holder:'CLAUDE_OPUS',run_id:'session_015nBJM7SgZNm63MtpxVNsVg'}) granted the lock, and evaluateTransition('READY','RUNNING_WRITER',{item_id:'ACP-002',writer_lock:<granted>}) returns ok=true. The same call without the lock is refused with WRITER_LOCK_NOT_HELD, and a second run claiming the held lock is refused with WRITER_LOCK_HELD — so the single-writer rule is enforced, not merely asserted.
One active writer, one active program: ACP-002 is the only item in an in-flight status, and the board's own concurrency check would report MULTIPLE_IN_FLIGHT_ITEMS if that stopped being true.
